newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian T-bond tender possible this week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian T-bond tender possible this week.

text.p: An Australian Treasury bond tender is seen as a possiblity this week, and there were rumours circulating the market that it could incorporate a new line of 2009 stock, traders said.
"There's a lot of rumours going around about a tender, and a new line is one of them," said one trader at a local bank.

The establishment of a 2009 stock was first muted by the Treasury in the budget papers on August 20 and would extend the yield curve beyond the August 2008 bond, currently the longest Treasury bond on issue.

"We're hearing that there is going to be a new line. They (the Treasury) would want to do at least A$600 or A$700 million of the new stock, which could make the whole tender to A$1.0 billion," said one trader at a European based bank.

Market soundings were taken when a 2009 issue was first considered and the response then was that there should be sufficient liquidity built up in the August 2008 line before going ahead, a Treasury official told Reuters.

"We feel now that we have sufficiently built up the 2008 to consider introducing a new line...so it is an option," the Treasury official said, adding that a tender announcement today was a possibility.

"There seems to be a good measure of support for that (2009 stock) in terms of maintaining the length of the yield curve and planning ahead for entry into the futures basket further down the track," the official added.
The Treasury last tendered on October 8 when its offered A$200 million of January 2001 and A$400 million of November 2006 stocks.
If a tender does go ahead this week, details will be announced at 1200 p.m. (0100 GMT) today.
Final bids would be due at 12.45 p.m. (0145 GMT) on Tuesday with the result announcement at 2.00 p.m. (0300 GMT).
